6-add-random-unjudged-pictures-as-backgr.line: Cheap and offline on idea 4's harness, and it picks which classifier idea 5 puts in front of a person. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Idea 4 found the gain comes from using the rejects; adding plain background negatives is the next step in the same direction and changes what idea 5 tests.
why.odds: Review rejects are near-misses, so background negatives plausibly help the library-wide top 100, but idea 4's held-out test cannot show that by itself.
why.path: Idea 4's harness and exported data are ready; idea 5 should use whichever variant wins.

10-add-a-random-batch-to-the-person-judg.line: Run inside idea 5's blind review: idea 4's win is on hand-picked pictures, and only a random batch shows whether that holds on the open library.

why.impact: Idea 2 found a strong model confirming new pictures at the random rate, so this control decides whether idea 5's numbers mean anything.
why.odds: Adding a random batch to a review is easy and almost certain to give a usable baseline.
why.path: Shares idea 5's review, so it sits just before it.

5-a-person-judges-the-classifier-s-top-1.line: Now the deciding test: idea 4 won clearly on 7 of 20 tags held out, but a vote over judged pictures tied it, so the person should judge that vote's list too. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Confirms on unjudged pictures are the issue's own success measure, and it decides whether to ship the classifier or the simpler judged-only vote.
why.odds: Raised from low: idea 4 beat the shipped vote by 20-30 points in the top 50 on content tags like jewelry and teeth, though only among pictures someone chose to review, and idea 2 warns that such wins can vanish on new pictures.
why.path: Should use idea 6's winner and carry idea 10's random batch.

9-a-stronger-picture-embedding-for-tags-.line: Its trigger has happened: in idea 4 every method sat close to chance on defect tags while content tags worked. Not yet judged.

why.impact: It would open the fine-grained tags, but those are mostly the anomaly tagger's own, and a larger embedding costs storage and a library pass.
why.odds: Idea 1's DINOv3 probe put 56 to 74 true positives in its top 100 for defect tags, but with about 1,200 labels rather than 100.
why.path: Can run now on idea 4's harness; nothing waits on it.

7-combine-the-classifier-and-the-near-ne.line: Weakened by idea 4: the judged-only vote tied the classifier on every tag, so combining them likely adds little. Not yet judged.

why.impact: If the two rankers agree, a combination ships no better than either alone.
why.odds: Idea 4 found the classifier and the judged-only vote within each other's spread on every tag.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; idea 5's overlap count between lists would show the same thing for free.

11-use-the-base-rate-thresholds-as-the-n.line: Probably already answered: idea 4 ran the shipped near-neighbour kernel copied unchanged. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Only a methodological check; idea 4's report already lists the vote's coverage per tag (the share scoring above zero).
why.odds: Using the shipped code is what idea 4 did, so it holds.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; read idea 4's report before spending a session on it.

12-have-a-person-judge-the-vote-s-top-10.line: Settles idea 3's open verdict but barely touches the main question, and costs a person's judging; could ride along in idea 5's review.

why.impact: It only decides which version of the shipped vote is the baseline, and idea 4 shows the bigger issue is that vote ignoring rejects.
why.odds: The two lists differ only where the old 55% bar lets fewer than 100 through, so a difference is likely on the rarest tags and nowhere else.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; sharing idea 5's review would save a separate judging session.

8-pick-the-next-pictures-to-judge-by-the.line: Last: idea 2 found a held-out model's ranking no better than random, and this only speeds up a classifier that must work first.

why.impact: It saves verdicts but does not answer whether the classifier works.
why.odds: Idea 2 concluded negative: ranked batches confirmed at the random rate, and the score did not order positives (AUC 0.49).
why.path: Should wait for idea 5 to show the classifier finds new examples at all.
